title: Architecture
body: The pipeline is: load the JSON files, check the built-in and kind schemas, build the reference graph, run the rules (block codes and the version hashes of links and code tags among them), render, and compare the output folder. ^ARC-1
The code is one Rust crate with a single binary and a small set of modules under `src`. ^ARC-2
packages: loader: a strict JSON parser that keeps offsets, positions and duplicate keys. ^ARC-4
config: reads `docc.json` and resolves effective levels. ^ARC-5

schema: compiles JSON Schema (draft 2020-12), restricts references to the schemas folder and maps errors to source positions. `kind.rs` reads a kind schema: whether it is strict, the allowed top-level names, `x-docc-target` and `x-docc-covered`. ^ARC-6
mdscan and text: scanners for code blocks, references with their version hashes, includes, block codes, words and sentences. ^ARC-7

engine: loads a project and runs all checks, including the graph and the suppressions. `versions.rs` computes the version hashes of targets and reports DOC209 with the change found in Git, `trace.rs` the fingerprints of code (DOC402), `migrate.rs` gives codes to blocks and moves a project of the old format; `lock.rs` only reads an old `docc.lock` for the move. ^ARC-8
rules: the registry of all rules; explain, rules and the skill are built from it. ^ARC-9

render: Markdown pages, the tree, the single Markdown file, the HTML application (`app.js` with Preact and htm from `vendor`, fed with a JSON island), numbering and images. `lang.rs` holds the Russian labels for `"lang": "ru"`. ^ARC-10

history: reads the Git history of the documents (one `git log` and one `git cat-file --batch`) and follows every block through it with the one alignment of blocks, `ops`, which the HTML history, `docc log` and `docc diff` share; changes: the output of `docc log` and `docc diff`; comments: the readers' comments in `$comments`, their shape (DOC112) and place (DOC215), the in-place edit of `docc comments apply` and the export of the HTML file. ^ARC-11
trace and report: `docc:` tags in code files, and the text and JSON reports. ^ARC-12

source: where the files of a project are read from, the disk or the tree of a Git revision (`docc compile --rev`, with `git ls-tree` and one `git cat-file --batch` for many files); config, schema, engine, trace and render read every file through it. ^ARC-13
cli: the command line; its flags behave as those of the Go version, which docc was first written in. The changes of the move to Rust are listed in `docs/rust-port`. ^ARC-14
principles: Golden tests, a pure core with input and output at the edges, and stable codes. The main dependencies are jsonschema, regex, comrak (it parses the Markdown of the single HTML file; docc writes the HTML itself), icu_collator for sorting titles and unicode-normalization. ^ARC-15
